requirements.condition: First pin the exact positive numeric IDs, selected-repository mode, and closed least-privilege permission maps for both governance Apps in immutable desired state. Install the Check App on every required-check repository and the Writer App on exactly the authority external-ledger target plus every template/consumer mutation target. Route authority governance-mirror credentials only to the exact template-mirror, authority governance-external-ledger credentials only to the authority repository itself, and each template/consumer governance-upgrade credential only to its own repository. Keep ID/private-key secrets in the exact named environments, prove repository/org governance-secret fallbacks are canonically empty, and complete a credential-environment-to-target installation token-mint/capability/permission probe. The signed observation must be no older than 3600 seconds.
requirements.reason: Rulesets, protected Check App verdicts, Writer App-authored propagation PRs, and protected external-ledger writes cannot be bound to unresolved or substituted App identities, wrong credential-to-target routes, overprivileged or all-repository App registrations, missing or extra installations, misplaced fallback secrets, secret metadata without working values, or stale hidden-state observations.

requirements.condition: Materialize and read back the existing signed release-tag authorization policy for the finalization path. Under PRODUCTION_GRADE_SINGLE_OWNER_SMALL_TEAM, one governed release-tag-authorizer is sufficient and must remain separate from the stage-only OIDC publisher, model, and candidate authority. Under MAXIMUM_ASSURANCE_MULTI_CUSTODIAN_WORM, at least two independently administered authorizers are required. The exact signed authorization remains bound to tag, tag object, commit, tree, registry, policy, TTL, and nonce.
requirements.reason: Finalization signer separation is an engineering trust decision enforced by the existing signed release authorization; multi-custodian quorum is an explicit maximum-assurance control and neither profile depends on a GitHub User/Team approval gate.

requirements.condition: Readback-align every managed ruleset (including active fleet/immutable-release-tags required_signatures as signed-commit defense-in-depth), required check App ID, protected environment, protected-main workflow identity, and immutable-releases setting; every release ref must independently resolve through the Git Tags API to the same verified signed annotated tag object and exact protected-main commit.
requirements.reason: A required_signatures ruleset does not by itself prove the annotated tag object's signature; release authority is withheld until both actual GitHub policy and the exact verified tag object are read back.

requirements.condition: Provision RELEASE_TAG_READ_TOKEN with repository Contents: read and no write permission for tag ref/object rechecks in the contents-writer job; separately allow RELEASE_TRUST_PREFLIGHT_TOKEN to read repository metadata, rulesets, check runs, Actions workflow runs, environments, secret metadata, App metadata, and immutable-release state without any write permission.
requirements.reason: A 403/404 caused by insufficient observation authority is indistinguishable from absent trust state and therefore fails closed.

requirements.condition: Before any template-mirror mutation can participate in release, a high-authority observer/proxy with ruleset-write observation authority must read back the exact ajenchen/design-system repository identity/default branch, complete rulesets with an empty bypass_actors set, required checks, Actions workflow permissions, and governance-mirror environment policy. PRODUCTION_GRADE_SINGLE_OWNER_SMALL_TEAM permits an owner-administered observer credential while preserving namespace isolation; MAXIMUM_ASSURANCE_MULTI_CUSTODIAN_WORM requires an independently administered observer/proxy. It must sign only the closed SHA-256 claims defined by the bound GitHub mutation-boundary contract, including the public ruleset projection over id, name, target, source_type, source, enforcement, created_at, updated_at, node_id, conditions, and rules. The observer credential must never enter GitHub Actions, model, or candidate namespaces; only signed claim output may cross that boundary.
requirements.reason: GitHub can hide bypass_actors from a caller without ruleset-write observation authority, so a runtime metadata:read token cannot directly prove that bypass is empty. The signed high-authority snapshot and its contract-bound public projection, including ruleset IDs and created/updated timestamps, let the low-authority runtime detect semantic or bypass-only freshness drift without receiving the observer credential.

requirements.condition: Mirror every GitHub reconcile transaction journal, recovery observation, rollback authorization, compensation result, and exact read-back receipt to an independently administered append-only off-host durable store; bind the approved adapter, HTTPS endpoint, tenant/container, WORM lifecycle, distinct writer/verifier principals, nonce, idempotent transaction/sequence/event key, and Ed25519 receipt key; then verify signed content digests and minimum retention by live read-back.
requirements.reason: Local fsync and atomic rename protect a workstation crash boundary but do not survive host loss, operator compromise, or local evidence deletion.

requirements.condition: In a first protected-main PR with no release authority, land the reviewed managed-CI workflow, contract/schema, plan/schema, trusted library/verifier, executor-image supply-chain, trusted-authority and host-sandbox policies, canonical manifest, current control-plane lock, and OIDC/broker policies. A protected freeze authority must create one content-addressed frozen-subject artifact whose locator, artifact id, digest, size, canonical manifest bytes, coverage, shards, source commit/tree, workflow run/attempt, authority OIDC projection, and lineage are exact; every execution class must download the same artifact and independently recompute its artifact and manifest-byte digests. Candidate-running jobs must have id-token:none and no signer, broker, credential, host namespace, container-engine socket, daemon socket, or parent-process visibility. Only protected authority environments may mint immutable-environment-subject OIDC tokens, authorize sandbox/egress sessions, broker secrets, and finalize receipts. Execution must use independently verified digest-pinned images bound to protected source/build recipe/context/materials, SBOM, SLSA provenance, Sigstore identity/bundle, and registry readback. An independently administered host sandbox must enforce read-only candidate mounts, separate outputs, per-class network namespace/firewall/authenticated proxy policy, and every negative write/socket/egress/namespace/ambient-secret probe. The protected finalizer must consume one closed class-complete rawReceiptSet carrying the actual bounded bytes for each canonical {executionClass}.json, reject missing or extra classes and path/digest/size drift, validate the exact raw schema and source-validator digest, class/evidence/run/envelope/OIDC/generated-output/dependency/runner/containment bindings, lifecycle, independent runtime-issuer quorum, and signer separation before deriving each finalized signing payload; its closed response must echo the request binding and return exactly one finalized payload, validation readback, and audit event per class. A retained two-hop transport readback must bind the exact request, raw-receipt-set, and finalized-receipt-set digests; prove WebPKI-verified TLS 1.3 plus GitHub OIDC from client to gateway and TLS 1.3 mTLS with exact gateway/signer identities from gateway to signer; and prove the gateway never held the signer private key. The receipt signer readback must exactly bind service, tenant, endpoint, key/certificate identity, OIDC trust policy, workflow/environment, payload schema/domain, append-only audit event, and runtime issuer-registry mapping. Model-broker authority must bind exact requested/observed model release identity, four closed signed authority/source/revocation/audit documents bound to the canonical registry, and unique per-exchange shard/provider-run/raw-response-digest observations inside signed release/invocation windows without relying on wall-clock revalidation. Independent runtime issuers and completion attestors must read back all projections, four-class receipts, zero release mutations, and mechanically recomputed full-provenance, per-class receipt/authority/image/freeze/host/signer/model-authority, and aggregate readback digests.
requirements.reason: A null or stale activation bundle, candidate-owned verifier, github.sha ambiguity, same-candidate workflow, mutable OIDC subject, reused JWT id, candidate-accessible token/signer/broker/host capability, substituted frozen artifact or manifest bytes, missing per-class recomputation, malicious digest-pinned image without exact supply-chain evidence, self-reported containment, failed negative probe, caller-authored receipt digest or readback, missing or extra raw receipt, raw-byte/path/schema/validator substitution, class/run/envelope/OIDC/output detachment, downgraded or detached finalization transport, mismatched request/raw-set/finalized-set digest, gateway-held signer key, same-key raw and final signing, signer without external service/certificate/audit/issuer mapping, model invocation outside signed authority/release windows, stale or bypassed model revocation/audit readback, unbound or replayed shard/provider-run/raw-response observation, opaque or replayed receipt, stale run attempt, or unbound network/secret policy cannot authorize release or fleet rollout.
